previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease status post renal transplant was admitted for hypertensive urgency, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He had been unable to take his oral medications due to gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to severely elevated blood pressure. He was initially managed in the ICU with intravenous antihypertensives and then transitioned to oral therapy. Renal ultrasound revealed new-onset renal artery stenosis, contributing to his hypertension and graft dysfunction. A tunneled hemodialysis catheter was placed on hospital day 1, and he began hemodialysis on day 2, completing three sessions with good tolerance. His nausea improved with dialysis. Medication changes included discontinuation of CellCept and Lasix, continuation of tacrolimus and prednisone, uptitration of doxazosin, and transition of calcitriol and epogen to in-center administration. He was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for ongoing outpatient dialysis and follow-up.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis
presenting with fever, chills.

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior exams, the most recent dated ___.

AP UPRIGHT CHEST:  A right subclavian catheter terminates in the proximal
right atrium. Heart size is normal.  The lungs are clear without effusion,
consolidation or pneumothorax.  Pulmonary vascularity is within normal limits.

IMPRESSION:  No radiographic evidence of pneumonia.

INDICATION:  Exchange of indwelling right tunneled hemodialysis catheter
secondary to presumed line infection.  Patient has end-stage renal disease, on
chronic hemodialysis.

PHYSICIANS:  Drs. ___ performed the procedure, with Dr.
___ attending physician who was present and supervising throughout
the entire procedure.

ANESTHESIA:  Moderate sedation was provided by administering divided doses of
50 mcg of fentanyl and 1 mg of Versed, with a total in-service time of 30
minutes, during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored.  Local anesthesia was established with 1% lidocaine.

TECHNIQUE AND FINDINGS:  After the risks, benefits, and alternatives of the
proposed procedure were explained to the patient, informed written consent was
obtained.  The patient was placed supine on the angiography table, with the
right neck, including the indwelling right tunneled hemodialysis catheter,
prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A preprocedure timeout was
then performed.

Both ports of the indwelling hemodialysis catheter were aspirated.  A 0.035
Stiff Glidewire was then advanced into both ports of the indwelling
hemodialysis catheter and advanced until the tip was in the IVC. Subsequently,
blunt dissection was performed at the entry site of the indwelling catheter to
free the cuff.  The indwelling catheter was then removed over the wires.  A
new 15.5 ___, 19 cm tip- to- cuff hemodialysis catheter, was then advanced
over the wires through the existing tunnel tract, and positioned with the tip
at the level of the right atrium. Both wires were removed. The ports were
aspirated and flushed. 0 silk was used x2 to suture the catheter in place.  A
sterile dressing was applied. The patient tolerated the procedure well without
immediate post- procedural complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated exchange of an indwelling right tunneled
hemodialysis catheter for a new 15.5 ___, 19 cm tip-to-cuff hemodialysis
catheter.  The tip is in the right atrium, and the catheter is ready to use.

INDICATION:  ___ male with end-stage renal failure.  Please evaluate
for first time HD access.

FINDINGS:  Both brachial arteries are singular and have normal bi/triphasic
waveforms.  The central subclavian veins are cardio and respirophasic and
symmetric side-to-side.

On the right, the cephalic vein is patent with diameters from wrist to
antecubital ranging from 1.9-2.2 mm.  From the antecubital to upper arm, the
cephalic vein diameters are 2.7, 1.8, 2.7 mm.  The right basilic vein is
patent with diameters ranging from antecubital fossa to upper arm of 2.7, 3.0,
3.1 mm respectively.

On the left, the cephalic vein is sub-1-mm in size and visualized only in the
mid upper arm.  The left basilic vein is patent with small diameters ranging
from 1.8-2.3 mm.

IMPRESSION:  Patent central veins.  Patent brachial arteries.  Small left-
sided veins.  Borderline right-sided veins were accessed.
